handbookNote: Missouri Commercial Driver License Manual (base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System' content, Version: July 2017, with Missouri-specific front matter and Section 11/12 modernized components revised March 2025, cover revised August 2025), published by the Missouri Department of Revenue (DOR) in cooperation with the Missouri State Highway Patrol (which administers CDL knowledge and skills testing) -- fetched directly from https://dor.mo.gov/forms/CDL%20Manual.pdf on 2026-08-22 (3.7MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext to scratchpad/mo_cdl_research/mo_cdl_manual_full.txt, 10,344 lines, cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction to resolve two-column table misalignment). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics, confirmed directly and unambiguously from the official Missouri-specific Section 14 front matter of this manual (a full, non-hedged disclosure unlike several other CDL-track states in this project, e.g. Louisiana, Alabama, Arkansas, Kansas, Indiana, Maine): General Knowledge test 50 questions; Air Brake test 25 questions; Combination Vehicle test 20 questions; Hazardous Materials Endorsement test 30 questions; Double/Triple Trailer Endorsement test 20 questions; Passenger Endorsement test 20 questions; Tank Endorsement test 20 questions; School Bus test 20 questions. You must score 80 percent on each exam (also the federally standardized minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a)). Missouri's CDL Skills Test consists of a pre-trip inspection, a Basic Vehicle Control Skills exam, and an On-Road Driving test, administered in that order only by appointment through Missouri State Highway Patrol Troop Headquarters; a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) must be held at least 14 calendar days before the skills test and is valid for one year (360 days), non-renewable. Missouri's three CDL vehicle classes are A (combination, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle or combination, GVWR 26,001+ lbs, towed unit 10,000 lbs GVWR or less), and C (vehicle not meeting A/B, but designed for 16+ passengers including driver, or hazmat-placarded, or carrying a 42 CFR Part 73 select agent/toxin). Missouri's six CDL endorsements are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank), P (Passenger), T (Double/Triple Trailer), X (combined Tank/Hazmat), and S (School Bus) -- Missouri does not use a separate charter-bus 'C' endorsement. Only Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank (N) endorsements may be added to a CLP. Missouri CDL eligibility: age 18 for intrastate (until 21), 21 for interstate; Missouri residency and two forms of address verification required; a Hazardous Materials endorsement requires a TSA/FBI fingerprint-based security threat assessment renewed at every CDL renewal. Mandatory FMCSA Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT), confirmed electronically, is required before hazmat/passenger/school-bus knowledge or skills testing, or before a first-time CDL or classification upgrade. CDL fees: written test $25, skills test $25, document issuance $9 (3 years or less) or $18 (3 years 1 day to 6 years); CLP $10. A limited military exemption under RSMo 302.720 allows the Director of Revenue to waive the CDL written and/or skills test for qualifying current or former U.S. armed forces members. Commercial license examinations are administered only in English with no interpreter permitted. Content-depth rationale: Missouri uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized/2005 CDL Testing System' base manual as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts), organized into the same core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes, endorsements/restrictions, disqualifications, other CDL rules), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing, communicating, speed/space management, seeing hazards, distracted driving, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, and mountain driving; 03_driving_safely_b covering driving emergencies, ABS, skid control/recovery, accident procedures, fires, alcohol/drugs, staying alert, and hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (split into two buckets for volume), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection (Missouri's modernized version, revised March 2025, with Class A/B/C skills-test checklists), Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving (12 and 13 combined into one bucket), plus Missouri-specific administrative detail from Section 14 layered into the licensing bucket. Some sections (Cargo, Tank Vehicles, Doubles/Triples) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Missouri manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers. The source PDF's two-column body layout was found to misorder some tabular numbers when extracted with pdftotext -layout (e.g. the Section 14 written-exam item-count table appeared row-shifted by one entry); all such numeric claims were cross-verified against a pdftotext -raw extraction, which preserves the PDF's true content-stream reading order, before being used in any question or in this note.
